column1: # TITLE: Identification of Myc target genes in xenograft tissue derived from human lung cancers
# SUMMARY: All three transforming members of the Myc family play a significant role in the development of both SCLC and NSCLC. NSCLC constitutes 80% of all lung cancer
column2: and cMyc expression is most often deregulated
column5: although we are interested in understanding the regulation and function of the entire Myc family in all lung cancers
column6: we focused our research on cMyc deregulation in NSCLC. To identify target genes whose regulatory regions are bound in response to deregulated cMyc in NSCLC
column7: we analyzed mouse xenograft tumours established in immune-compromised mice from monolayer cell lines derived from primary adenocarcinoma NSCLCs. These xenografts were chosen for further study because they show a genetic profile similar to their respective primary tumour (MGH8
column10: MGH24). High c-myc expression positively correlates with the ability of NSCLC cell lines to form xenografts
column11: suggesting that Myc contributes towards the ability of the cells to grow in vivo. We conducted Myc-specific ChIP-chip and the corresponding normal IgG control using the Agilent genome-wide oligonucleotide promoter arrays on 3 biological replicates
column12: of each of the four xenograft tumours. Following pre-processing using variance-stabilizing normalization and statistical analysis using general linear models we identified a list of 2
column13: 207 genes significantly enriched for c-Myc binding.
